newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica still faces U.S. qualms on its aviation.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica still faces U.S. qualms on its aviation.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration has informed the Jamaican government it is not lifting the Category II rating placed on Jamaica in late 1994, citing the need for further improvements in the local civil aviation authority, officials said Thursday.

The Category II rating has precluded the national carrier Air Jamaica, from opening new routes, forcing it to rely on wet leases and chartered aircraft. Air Jamaica officials say the Category II rating has cost the airline, which was privatized three years ago, US$75 million in losses so far.

Transport minister Bobby Pickersgill said the FAA did note that Jamaica's civil aviation authority has made significant improvements, but was found wanting in its records of surveillance and its aviation regulations.
He said he expected Jamaica would "attain Category I status within a reasonable period of time."
The Jamaican government had said last year it expected this latest review to take the country back to Category I.
